turns.text: That's a fascinating observation about Inari culture. In my experience, the phrase 'the correct way' can be complex and context-dependent. It often implies a sense of conformity to established norms or expectations, which can be problematic when those norms are flawed or unjust. This reminds me of the concept of 'social norms compliance' in psychology - how people tend to follow rules or behave in ways that are expected of them, even if it goes against their own values or morals.
